In contrast to Harrisburg's good record in unemployment, it does have problems with family income levels. Harrisburg has a high concentration of families in lower income brackets. In Harrisburg, 19 percent of the families had an income of $4,000 or less, while state-wide, only 12 percent of the families had incomes below $4,000. At the same time, 28 percent of the families had incomes between $10,000 and $15,000; the figure for Harrisburg is 23 percent. Hence, Harrisburg is poorer in that not only is the medium income lower, but the whole income distribution picture has shifted downward. For example, 14.9 percent of all families in Harrisburg have incomes below the poverty level, as indicated by Table 11 below, while this is true for only 4 percent of the families in the balance of the Harrisburg SMSA.
